04-129.r: Hunger persists despite three-fold rise in foodgrains (1950-1990) → Green Revolution limited to small pockets, food costly versus earnings of poor, wheat/paddy favoured over coarse grains.

04-130.r: Maximum Green Revolution benefit → Punjab, Haryana and Western Uttar Pradesh (good irrigation and infrastructure); began with Kharif crop in 1966.

04-131.r: PM's Second Green Revolution → global agri trade for farmers, less post-harvest wastage, better crop storage; not encouraging FDI in agriculture.

04-132.r: Eco-friendly farming practice → organic farming (compost, green manure, crop rotation; no synthetic fertilizers or pesticides).

04-133.r: Soil Health Card Scheme (19 February 2015, Suratgarh, Rajasthan) → checks overuse of fertilizers by advising nutrient doses; not irrigation or bank loans.

04-134.r: INSIMP (2011-12, under RKVY) → demonstrates millet production, post-harvest and value-addition technologies with cluster approach; poor, small, marginal, tribal farmers have larger stake.

04-135.r: National Agriculture Technology Project (NATP, 1998, ICAR) → funded by the World Bank.

04-136.r: First Krishi Vigyan Kendra → 1974 at Puducherry; KVKs are part of the National Agricultural Research System.

04-137.r: PMFBY (13 January 2016, from Kharif 2016; replaced NAIS and MNAIS) → covers post-harvest losses from cyclones and unseasonal rains; premium not uniform two percent.

04-138.r: First crop insurance → Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme, 1 April 1985 (Kharif season).

04-139.r: National Agricultural Insurance Scheme → from Rabi 1999-2000, replacing Comprehensive Crop Insurance Scheme (April 1, 1985); covers crop failure from calamities, pests, diseases.

04-142.r: Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme → first in Karnataka (Kharif 2007); extended to 10 States from Kharif 2008.

04-143.r: Varsha Bima (rainfall insurance) → run by Agriculture Insurance Company of India (true); introduced in 2004 South-West monsoon, not 2007 (false).
04-143.t: Don't confuse Varsha Bima (2004) with Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme (Kharif 2007).

04-144.r: Crop insurance monopoly at question time → Agriculture Insurance Company of India (AIC); till 2002-03 run by General Insurance Corporation.
04-144.c: Book gives no single answer: at question time crop insurance lay with the Agriculture Insurance Company of India (AIC), not an option; GIC ran it only until 2002-03.

04-145.r: Correct → Crop Insurance Scheme 1985; Uttar Pradesh has 9 agro-climatic zones; Food for Work 1977. Wrong → Blue Revolution is fish, not mustard.

04-146.r: Hariyali scheme (January 2003, PM Vajpayee; Rs. 2000 crore) → water harvesting / watershed management; under Ministry of Rural Development.

04-148.r: Vishesh Krishi Upaj Yojana → boost export of fruits, vegetables, flowers, minor forest produce, dairy, poultry; exporters get duty credit scrip (5 percent of FOB).

04-150.r: PM-KUSUM (2019) → end farmers' dependence on diesel and kerosene; link pump sets to solar energy; supports 40% non-fossil power capacity by 2030.

04-152.r: National Land Records Modernization Programme → launched 2008 to digitise land records; now Digital India Land Record Modernization Programme (DILRMP).

04-153.r: Watershed Development Fund (2000) → Rs. 200 crore (Rs. 100 crore each, Agriculture Ministry and NABARD); 100 selected districts; 'two-thirds for grants' false.

04-154.r: Rainfed Area Development Programme → 2011-12, sub-scheme of RKVY; full package of activities to maximise farm returns of small and marginal farmers.

04-155.r: PMKSY (1 July 2015, 'Har Khet Ko Paani') → assured irrigation, water use efficiency; repairing water bodies, wells, aquifer recharge, rain harvesting all included.
hi: Har Khet Ko Paani (हर खेत को पानी)

04-156.r: Uttar Pradesh Diversified Agriculture Support Project (UPDASP) → World Bank-sponsored; Phase-I began 23 September 1998.

04-157.r: Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (1996-97) → central loans to States for near-complete irrigation projects, not poor farmers; Command Area Development (1974-75) → efficient irrigation use.

04-158.r: Suraj Dhara Yojana (Madhya Pradesh) → seed exchange; certified seeds for SC/ST farmers to shift to oilseeds and pulses.

04-159.r: Atal Bhujal Yojana (Atal Jal) → Rs. 6,000 crore scheme; World Bank share Rs. 3,000 crore (450 million US $), approved June 2018; launched 1 April 2020.

04-161.r: Jaldhara Yojana → pump sets to poor desert farmers at nominal rent or lease.

04-162.r: Largest area under tube-well irrigation → Uttar Pradesh.

04-163.r: Handbook of Agriculture → published by ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research).

04-164.r: Uttar Pradesh Council of Agricultural Research → Lucknow (established 1989).

04-165.r: Krishak Samridhi Aayog (Uttar Pradesh) → November 2017, to suggest ways of doubling farmers' income by 2022; chaired by the Chief Minister.

04-166.r: NAFED (2 October 1958) → apex body of agricultural marketing cooperatives; under Ministry of Agriculture.

04-168.r: Not an agri-export agency → IFFCO (fertilizers); NAFED, State Trading Corporation and MMTC export agricultural goods.

04-169.r: Agricultural markets regulated by State APMC Acts (agriculture is a State List subject); APMCs regulate sale and collect market fees.
hi: Agricultural Produce Market Committee (कृषि उपज मंडी समिति)

04-170.r: Golden rice → genetically engineered to make beta-carotene (precursor of vitamin A), for areas short of dietary vitamin A.

04-171.r: Demand for agricultural products → inelastic (people buy little more even when price falls).

04-172.r: First agricultural university → G.B. Pant University, Pantnagar (inaugurated 1960 as 'Uttar Pradesh Agricultural University'; renamed 1972).

04-173.r: Pantnagar university → inaugurated by Nehru, 17 November 1960 (statement I true); statement on six colleges in 1901-1905 is false.

04-174.r: ICAR projects in order → Krishi Vigyan Kendra (1974), Lab to Land (1979), NATP (1998), National Agricultural Innovation Project (2006).

04-175.r: Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR) → Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.

04-176.r: Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI) → Mysuru (Mysore), Karnataka; established 1950.

04-177.r: National Academy of Agricultural Research Management (NAARM) → Hyderabad, Telangana; established 1976.

04-178.r: Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute → Jhansi, Uttar Pradesh; established 1962.

04-179.r: International Potato Centre (CIP, founded 1971) → headquarters Lima, Peru; works on potato, sweet potato, Andean roots and tubers.

04-180.r: Neeru-Meeru ('water and you') water-harvesting programme → Andhra Pradesh, 2000.

04-181.r: Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) → sugarcane; replaced Statutory Minimum Price from 2009-10 (Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966 amended 22.10.2009).

04-183.r: FRP of sugarcane approved by Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), on CACP's recommendation, after consulting States and sugar industry.
04-183.t: CACP only recommends the FRP; the CCEA approves it.

04-184.r: FCI economic cost of foodgrains → acquisition cost (MSP + bonus + procurement incidentals) + distribution cost.

04-185.r: MSP procurement is not unlimited for all crops, and MSP does not cap market prices → neither true; MSP covers 24 commodities (7 cereals, five pulses, 8 oilseeds...).

04-188.r: Niger (ramtil, Guizotia abyssinica) → Kharif crop with MSP (one of 14 kharif MSP crops); some tribal people cook with its oil (all three true).

04-189.r: Since 1997-98 → MSP > C2 cost (C2 = actual paid costs + imputed family labour + interest on owned capital + rental value of owned land).

04-190.r: MSP recommended by Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP): set up January 1965 as Agricultural Prices Commission, renamed CACP in 1985.

04-196.r: CACP objectives → stabilise farm prices, meaningful real income for farmers, protect consumers through PDS at reasonable rates; not 'maximum price for farmers'.

04-198.r: MSP → ensures minimum fixed price for farmers and helps food security; farmers sell to government only when market price is below MSP; not for profit.

04-199.r: Wheat MSP when asked (2013) → Rs. 1350/quintal; RMS 2024-25 → Rs. 2275 (Rs. 150 above 2023-24's Rs. 2125).

04-200.r: Paddy (common) MSP 2018-19 → Rs. 1,750/quintal (Grade A Rs. 1770); 2024-25 → Rs. 2300 (up Rs. 117).

04-201.r: First State with MSP for fruits and vegetables → Kerala (decided October 2020, effective November 1, 2020; 16 commodities).

04-202.r: Groundnut MSP 1995-96 → Rs. 900/quintal; 2024-25 → Rs. 6783 per quintal.

04-203.r: Government buys foodgrains (for PDS and buffer stock) at Procurement Price, generally higher than MSP.

04-205.r: Not a cash crop among options → Soyabean; tobacco, cotton and rubber are cash crops.

04-206.r: Union Budget 2011-12 → prompt-repayment subvention raised from 2% to 3%, so farm loans (up to Rs. 3 lakh at 7%) effectively cost 4%.

04-207.r: Running cost capital of a farm → seeds, fertilizer, irrigation water (inputs); land revenue is not included.

04-208.r: Limited contribution to rural economy → practice of lending personal money; pastoralism, cottage industry and good tools contribute.

04-209.r: Principles of agricultural finance → purpose, person and productivity planning (all of the above).
04-209.h: Three Ps: Purpose, Person, Productivity planning.

04-210.r: Institutional farm credit → cooperative societies/banks, commercial banks, Regional Rural Banks, government; non-institutional → moneylenders, relatives. All options are sources → 'none of these'.
